title: Deac's Left Arm
scene: Night has dropped on a Kent school zone that still flashes for no one. You are second in a two-vehicle run: the Ledger ahead, amber destination sign dark, west-coast mirrors wide as doors. Deac's left arm comes out the driver's window, straight out, then down — the old transit slow. Radios are trash. This is the sentence. A third set of lamps sits on your bumper, too close, some volunteer who joined without asking. Gracie is boxed. Your job is not to be clever. Your job is to answer him without lighting the block.
decision: Deac's left arm is out and down. The volunteer behind you is tight. How do you answer?

options.text: Match him: left arm out and down, lift off, and open a gap ahead of the volunteer
options.result: You answer in kind. The Menace slows without the brake lamps dumping. The volunteer has to lift or eat your plow. He lifts. Deac's arm comes back in. The three of you roll the zone at twenty, dark and boring. That is a successful convoy.

options.text: Flash your headlights twice so Deac knows you saw it
options.result: The flashes bounce off his expanded-metal rear and paint the playground. Deac's arm stays down because he was not asking for a receipt. At the treeline, two shapes that were sitting stand up and start to walk the fence toward the light.

options.text: Tap the brakes hard so the volunteer gets the message
options.result: Your lamps dump red into his windshield. He stands on his own brakes. Three vehicles, one wet school zone, a squeal. Deac's arm comes back in and the destination sign flickers one word you cannot read from here. You just talked over him.

options.text: Pass him on the left and take the point — he is going too slow for the insulin
options.result: You pull out in a flashing school zone. His left arm is still in the air you are occupying. The Ledger's mirror almost takes your mesh. He never speeds up. You are now point on a road you have not searched, with a volunteer still glued to Deac, and no one behind you speaking the same language.

debrief: Left arm out, fingers pointing at the ground, means slow or stop. Answer with the same arm and a smooth lift. Deac was talking. A flash and a panic brake talk over him.

source.psdp_skill: Skill five: driving on a quiet street – part two
source.teaching_target: Left arm out and down means slow or stop; answer a convoy signal with the same hand signal and a smooth deceleration.

image_brief.subject: Deac's left arm out the Ledger's driver window as seen from behind, arm out and angled down, fingers pointing at the ground
image_brief.foreground: wet following-driver glass, a smear of rain, the Ledger's left rear quarter filling the frame
image_brief.midground: open driver window, west-coast mirror, the arm the column can actually see
image_brief.background: overcast night, flashing white school-zone lamps, empty playground fence
image_brief.read: the arm is out and down — stop — on the driver side a following vehicle can see
